A California Apple user has filed a class-action lawsuit accusing the company of misleading consumers about the privacy protections of its "Hide My Email" feature. Here are the details.

Apple sued over alleged "Hide My Email" vulnerability

Recently, 404 Media reported that Apple was aware of a so-called vulnerability more than a year ago that could potentially expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple's "Hide My Email" feature allows users to create unique, randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to their personal inboxes, letting them sign up for apps, websites, and newsletters without revealing their real address.

The feature is available for free through "Sign in with Apple," while a more comprehensive version included with the iCloud+ plan (starting at $0.99 per month) lets users create aliases for websites, newsletters, and other services.

According to 404 Media, a security researcher warned Apple in June 2025 of a vulnerability that could expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple acknowledged receiving the report about a month later, but allegedly never fixed the issue. In March 2026, the company said it had patched the vulnerability, but the researcher found it could still be exploited.

Quoting 404 Media:

Returning to the case itself (as reported by MacRumors), plaintiff Anthony Alvarez stated:

Apple was aware of the issue more than a year ago, yet the vulnerability remains unfixed — all while Apple has continued to profit from "Hide My Email" and its privacy promises. The plaintiff is one of millions of customers who pay Apple for iCloud+ and rely on Apple's claim that "Hide My Email" protects their personal email addresses. The plaintiff and class members have paid for Apple's privacy protection — iCloud+ users through the premium built into the iCloud+ subscription fee, and all Apple customers through the product premium built into Apple products that Apple touts as offering stronger privacy protections and features like "Hide My Email."

The lawsuit also claims this is not an isolated incident, citing a 2023 report that Apple's randomized MAC address feature could potentially expose users' real hardware identifiers.

The lawsuit also alleges that the total amount claimed by class members exceeds $5 million (excluding interest and legal costs), though it does not explain how that figure was calculated.

Alvarez filed the lawsuit on behalf of himself and other Apple customers he claims were similarly affected. He is asking the court to certify the case as a class action covering four proposed user groups:

  • A national Apple customer group — those who purchased a device and used "Hide My Email";
  • A California subgroup of the above users;
  • A national iCloud+ subscriber group — those who used the feature;
  • A California subgroup of iCloud+ subscribers.

He is requesting a jury trial and, in addition to monetary damages to be determined, is also asking the court to order Apple to fix "Hide My Email" or clearly disclose its limitations.

Apple has not yet responded to the lawsuit.

Do you think this class action should be certified? Let us know in the comments.
